content.figure_caption: Figure 8. Management of pulmonary oedema. MCS = mechanical circulatory support; RRT = renal replacement therapy; SBP = systolic blood pressure.
flowchart_summary: Initial: Oxygen (Class I) or ventilatory support (Class IIa).
If SBP ≥110 and no signs of hypoperfusion: Loop diuretics (Class I) and/or vasodilators (Class IIb).
If signs of hypoperfusion: Loop diuretics (Class I) and inotropes/vasopressors (Class IIb).
If SBP <110 or persistent instability: Loop diuretics (Class I).
Goal: Congestion relief. If congestion relieved → medical therapy optimization (Class I).
If congestion not relieved → consider RRT, MCS, other devices (Class IIa) or palliative care.
content.section_summary: Right ventricular (RV) failure is associated with increased RV and atrial pressure and systemic congestion. RV failure may impair left ventricular filling and reduce systemic cardiac output via ventricular interdependence.
therapeutic_recommendations: Diuretics are often first-line therapy for venous congestion.
Noradrenaline and/or inotropes are indicated for low cardiac output and haemodynamic instability.
Inotropes that reduce cardiac filling pressures may be preferred (example given: levosimendan, phosphodiesterase type III inhibitors).
Because inotropic agents may aggravate arterial hypotension, they can be combined with norepinephrine if needed.
